Subject: Children's ibuprofen recall (Corvane): what happened and what to do

This is Rania Haddad, pharmacist at Cedarbrook Pharmacy. Many of you have seen the post about children's ibuprofen bought here, so this is what's going on and what to do.

WHAT IS RECALLED
Corvane Pharma is recalling the dosing syringe packed in the box with Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (berry, 120 mL bottle), lots CV6114A and CV6114B. The lot number is on the bottom of the box.

The medicine itself is fine. It is not contaminated and not expired (expiry 08/2027). The problem is the printing on the syringe. Every mark is labelled at half of what it really measures: the line marked 2.5 mL holds 5 mL, and the line marked 5 mL holds 10 mL. A parent who followed the syringe gave about double the intended dose.

WHAT TO DO
1. Check the lot number on the bottom of the box. If it isn't CV6114A or CV6114B, your box is not part of this recall.
2. If it is one of those lots, stop using the syringe from the box and throw it out.
3. Come in for a correctly marked replacement syringe. They arrive today (Monday) before noon. They are free for anyone, no receipt needed.
4. If you'd rather not keep the product, bring it back for a full refund.

We are also opening extra this Saturday, Nov 14, from 10 to 4 for exchanges.

IF YOU ALREADY GAVE A DOSE WITH THAT SYRINGE
I can't judge this for your child over Facebook. It depends on their weight, how many doses they had, and their kidneys. If you have any doubt about how much was given, call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-800-268-9017. They will assess your child with you over the phone.

Don't give another dose of ibuprofen until the poison centre or a doctor tells you it's ok.

Call 911 or go to the ER right away if your child:
- is very sleepy or hard to wake
- is vomiting blood
- is not peeing
- has a seizure

WHY YOU DIDN'T GET A PHONE CALL
The recall notice reached us late on Friday, Nov 6. On Saturday morning we pulled the remaining bottles off the shelf and put signs on the front door and in the kids' aisle. This product is sold off the shelf without a prescription, so we have no name or phone number for the people who bought it. I can't call people I have no record of. That's why I'm posting here, and why I'm asking you to share this with any parent who shops in the area.

If you can't get through to us by phone, please come in. If your question is about a dose your child already had, don't wait for us. Call the poison centre.

Rania Haddad, Pharmacist
Cedarbrook Pharmacy
